To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
amphiphilic polymer ligands are effective for the preparation of highly active and selective heterogeneous catalysts for the biphasic catalytic reactions.

the use of amphiphilic plant polyphenol as ligand/stabilizing agent allows the preparation of novel noble metal complex and nanoparticle catalysts that can catalyze aqueous-organic phase reactions with high selectivity and reusability, and that the catalytic activity can be rationally tuned by adjusting the content of the polyphenols.

amphiphilic polymer-stabilized noble metal catalysts have been successfully developed and applied to the aqueous-organic catalysis of cimamaldehyde and 1-methylnaphthalene, which can be recycled for 3 times without loss of activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of novel amphiphilic catalysts that combine homogeneous and heterogeneous catalyst properties.
the development of novel catalyst systems for aqueous-organic catalysis.
the synthesis of amphiphilic catalysts and their application in the biphasic catalytic reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of polyphenol as ligand/stabiliser allows for the preparation amphiphilic noble metal catalysts that combine homogeneous catalytic activity and heterogeneous reusability, and the catalysts can catalyse a variety of biphasic organic reactions in aqueous- organic media.
the polyphenol-stabilized catalysts are promising candidates for the development of highly efficient biphasic catalysts.
the polyphenols-charged noble metal complex and nanoparticle catalysts are highly selective and active, and can be recycled at least 3 cycles without significant loss of catalytic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel strategy for the preparation of amphiphilic noble metal catalysts that are highly selective and active, and can be easily recycled in aqueous- organic biphasic catalytic systems.
the polyphenol-chelated noble metal catalysts can be applied in the biphasic catalytic reactions, which is of significance to industrial applications.
the amphiphilic nature of polyphenols can be exploited to design novel catalysts for aqueous biphasic catalytic reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of polyphenols as amphiphilics allows for the design of novel biphasic catalysts that combine homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis.
the use of polyphenols as amphiphillic ligand/stabilizers is a novel and effective approach to design highly active, selective and reusable catalysts.
the use of large amphiphilic molecules as ligands and stabilizers can be a general strategy to design highly selective and active catalysts for aqueous-organic phase catalysis.
